body.x: Marking its third edition this year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea's benchmark future industry exhibition, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," the expo establishes a new milestone for global industry by organically linking core technologies across four key advanced sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Encompassing the achievements of Daegu Metropolitan City's forward-looking industrial cultivation, leading domestic and international tech enterprises alongside promising startups will assemble to unveil next-generation, field-validated technologies poised to transform everyday life and industrial operations. Concurrently featuring international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation initiatives, the event is set to serve as a pivotal exchange hub leading technological collaboration and innovation far beyond Asia.

As an official Global Media Award partner for FIX 2026, Le Café du Geek is an influential French technology publication that delivers global tech news and comprehensive product reviews in French to readers across the Francophone world. It possesses strong capabilities in identifying innovative startups early to illuminate fresh business value, while also operating DroidSoft (droidsoft.fr), a specialized French mobile technology news portal. In particular, it has built solid credibility through a pragmatic evaluation methodology grounded in weeks of rigorous field testing inside real French households across the country. Beginning with DIFA 2023—one of the core expos consolidated into FIX—and continuing through FIX's inaugural 2024 edition and subsequent 2025 event, Le Café du Geek returns to Daegu this year to serve as a strategic bridge connecting South Korea's advanced AI, robotics, and future mobility technologies with France and broader European markets. An advance interview was conducted with Editor-in-Chief Léo Thévenet, invited to Daegu for the fourth consecutive year, to explore European perspectives on AI transformation and his expectations for FIX 2026.

body.x: 1. Could you introduce your media outlet to Korean readers?

Le Café du Geek is a French technology media outlet delivering global tech news in French, providing in-depth product reviews, and reporting daily industry developments. The team pays close attention to startup innovation, focusing on discovering emerging enterprises early to highlight the unique value they bring to the market. Alongside this, the organization operates DroidSoft (droidsoft.fr), a dedicated French smartphone news portal. Because the editorial team conducts real-world product testing across France, the Korean products reviewed undergo weeks of direct, hands-on usage in actual French home environments before evaluations are published. From smartphones to consumer appliances and mobility platforms, South Korean brands command a significant share of coverage, and readership remains keenly interested in the next wave of innovation originating from Korea.
2. What are your perspectives on current trends across industrial technology, mobility, and AI?

Every sector is advancing at a high pace, with the pace of change in artificial intelligence particularly extraordinary. AI models are developing genuine autonomy and operational execution capabilities. Moving beyond basic conversational Q&A, they now formulate plans and independently execute complex tasks. Capabilities that were entirely unfeasible just six months ago are operational realities today. This rapid development is reshaping industry and mobility as well: robots, vehicles, and factory floors grow smarter with each passing year, and technologies that once appeared as early-stage prototypes are transitioning into commercially available products in rapid succession. The remaining challenge is deploying these technologies in intuitive, cost-effective formats so that anyone can adopt and use them seamlessly.

body.x: 3. What key issues and topics related to FIX 2026 will interest your readership most?

The readership focuses primarily on practical technologies ready for immediate deployment or nearing everyday integration. Key interests include everyday artificial intelligence, electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, urban and service robotics, and new consumer smart devices. There is also substantial appetite for early-stage startup discovery, particularly when their products demonstrate viable potential for market entry across France and Europe.
4. How was your experience during FIX 2025, and what are your expectations for this year's exhibition?

FIX 2025 at EXCO in Daegu left a strong impression by bringing together 585 exhibiting companies and over 115,000 visitors, characterized by a sharp, unambiguous focus on AI. On-site coverage yielded numerous compelling narratives, resulting in multiple feature stories covering the overarching exhibition and award-winning enterprises. At this year's exhibition, the primary expectation is encountering an expanded array of market-ready products prepared for European expansion, alongside observing AI technologies integrated even more deeply across diverse industrial verticals.
5. What are your thoughts on the FIX Innovation Awards press conference?

The format was highly efficient, characterized by concise, high-density presentations, concrete physical products, and opportunities for direct Q&A with company founders. This operational structure enabled the precise selection of innovations most relevant to French readers, including solutions featured in dedicated standalone coverage such as PARKIE, Arion, and the EV Air Station by Hanwha Corporation E&C Division.

body.x: Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting from the front lines of technological developments by innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea's high-tech landscape.
